transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, this is Brett. Can I verify you with your account number and PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Brett, account 704-556-201, PIN 3390, name is Olivia Chen.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks Olivia, you're verified. What's happening today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My internet keeps dropping every few minutes, it's been going on for two days. I've restarted the router loads of times, I've checked all the cables, I've tried everything I can think of and nothing helps.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. When it drops, is it every device or just one, and what do the modem lights do?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's everything in the house, and the main light goes red for about thirty seconds then comes back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when did this start, was there anything that changed around then, new equipment or an update?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nothing that I can think of. It just started on its own about two days ago, out of nowhere.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Alright. Let's check the cable first. Unplug the one between the modem and your router at both ends and plug it back in firmly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay... unplugged both ends... pins look fine... plugging them back in. I heard a click on both.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fine. Now open your connection details and tell me the latency and any packet loss.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It says latency is about 160 milliseconds and packet loss is around 5 percent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right. And you said you've restarted the router already, how many times roughly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Honestly probably ten or fifteen times over the two days. It never sticks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Restarting it over and over like that is a stupid thing to keep doing, that was never going to fix anything. Just do exactly what I tell you from now on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Excuse me? There's really no need to talk to me like that, I'm just trying to explain what I tried.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm being honest with you. Change your DNS to 8.8.8.8 in the settings and stop messing with the router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't appreciate the attitude. Can you please just help me properly?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am helping you. Go into the network settings and change the DNS like I said.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. I've changed it to 8.8.8.8 and saved. It's still dropping though, same as before.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then try rebooting the modem this time instead of the router. Do it now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've rebooted the modem too. Waiting for it to come back... it's back, but it just dropped again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then it's your equipment, not us. There's not much else I can do.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So that's it? You're just going to leave it like this?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Try the DNS change again. Thank you for choosing S-Net.
